title: SSH: ML-KEM NISTP PQ hybrid KEX processing
description:
This MR introduces following changes:
- Adds `mlkem768nistp256-sha256` and `mlkem1024nistp384-sha384` to `ssh_dissect_kex_pq_hybrid`. This unifies dissection of all currently defined PQ hybrids and removes incomplete weird `ssh_dissect_kex_hybrid`
- Corrects PQ/T order - PQ actually comes before T in all SSH cases
- Explicitly defines all known relevant server and client key lengths to highlight discrepancies
- Parses length out of host signature data in Key Exchange Reply

Verified on OpenSSH (which supports `sntrup761x25519-sha512` and `mlkem768x25519-sha512` as well as AsyncSSH which supports all four PQ/T hybrids.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/21111/diffs?diff_id=1475719615&start_sha=956e78271f435d3f458cce66482c9be9755260c6#1bf6e4005e105405db89acc9c1073c2f14004190_1539_1539)

Where is key_name coming from?  If it's from packet data DISSECTOR_ASSERT_NOT_REACHED shouldn't be used.   DISSECTOR_ASSERT_XXX macros are for catching developer bugs, not "haven't yet implemented or typo in name".

I think this is actually correct application of `DISSECTOR_ASSERT_NOT_REACHED`. `ssh_dissect_kex_pq_hybrid` is called only for specific KEXes matches by exact same strings:

```
    else if (strcmp(kex_name, "sntrup761x25519-sha512") == 0 ||
        strcmp(kex_name, "mlkem768x25519-sha256") == 0 ||
        strcmp(kex_name, "mlkem768nistp256-sha256") == 0 ||
        strcmp(kex_name, "mlkem1024nistp384-sha384") == 0)
    {
        global_data->kex_specific_dissector = ssh_dissect_kex_pq_hybrid;
    }
```


So if `kex_name` is somehow something other than these four concrete values, there was introduced a bug in dissector.

What do you think?


`kex_name` is stored in `ssh_flow_data` aka `global_data->kex`.

Same as above... I think it's appropriate action as `ssh_dissect_kex_pq_hybrid` is only called for specific KEXes, not for arbitrary hybrids. After all, there is no good way to distinguish between unknown hybrid KEXes and unknown non-hybrids as they are just strings.
